Now the establishment parties (Conservatives and Labour) are currently in a coalition and will oppose any government Geert tries to form. The Christian democrats are the dutch version of Merkel's party and Democrats66 are pro-EU, so both of those will oppose Geert's government also. The Greens and the party for the animals are full of fanatical leftists, so they will also oppose Geert's government.

The Socialists are anti-EU, so it is likely that they would be willing to form a coalition, provided the Freedom party supports some socialist policies during the coalition. Christian Union and the Reformed party are Eurosceptic christian parties who can be easily persuaded into a coalition, especially as this would be their one opportunity to be in power.

So totalling the support and opposition seats we get 69 in support of Geert, and 83 opposed, with 8 unknowns (50 plus and independents). 81 seats out of 160 are needed to form government.
